To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) SC proliferation, as determined by cell counting and [H]thymidylate incorporation, and HA synthesis are enhanced in vitro by factors from KC and LEC conditioned media, and (ii) ET pretreatment increases the number of SC and the production of HA by the whole SC population.

(1) SC from ET-treated animals produce more HA than normal SC; (2) SC from ET-pretreated rats have a larger proliferative capacity; (3) conditioned media from KC and LEC, particularly from ET-pretreatened rats, stimulate HA synthesis and proliferation in SC.

(i) the number of isolated SC is higher in ET-treated than in normal animals, (ii) the SC from ET-treated rats are more responsive to the stimulatory effect of KC conditioned media than normal SC and (iii) the SC from normal and ET-treated rats respond differently to the conditioned media from LEC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the sinusoidal cells, in the pathophysiology of sepsis and endotoxic shock.
the influence of endotoxemia on the synthesis of HA by the SC population in culture.
the role of the liver in the production of plasma HA in endotoxemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SC of ET-treated animals are more active in producing HA and that the KC conditioned media contain factors that are able to stimulate the HA production by the SC.
ET and sepsis are capable to induce the proliferation of SC and the production of hyaluronan by the SC population in culture.
endotoxin, in addition to its known effects on the reticuloendo-thelial system, also affects the sinusoidal cells, and that this effect may be of clinical importance in the course of sepsis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SC population is activated in sepsis.
ET-treated rats have an increased potential to produce HA in the SC population and this is enhanced by the presence of mediators released by the reticuloendothyelial system.
SC are a major source for HA synthesis in endotoxin-induced sepsis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ET-treated rats have a greater potential to produce HA than normal rats, and that this is due to the increased yield of SC.

the SC are a major source of HA in the liver and that their proliferation and HA synthesis can be stimulated in vitro by factors from KC and LEC, and that these cells may be involved in the pathogenesis of sepsis-induced HA elevation in plasma.
ET and sepsis induce changes in the liver sinusoidal cells which are likely to be important for the pathogenesis of liver injury and the systemic inflammatory response syndrome.
